newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia opposition to debate govt effectiveness.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia opposition to debate govt effectiveness.

text.p: Slovenia's main opposition party said on Wednesday it had called for a parliamentary debate on the government's effectiveness -- a move that could eventually lead to a no-confidence vote.
The Social Democratic Party said it felt the government had been dragging its feet over the 1997 budget proposal, which has not yet been presented to parliament.
"The government...is thus obstructing normal activities of the state and local communities," the party said in a statement.
"We will decide whether to request a vote of no-confidence or not depending upon the course of the parliamentary debate," SDS' spokeswoman Nika Dolinar told Reuters.
The debate is expected to take place in September.
Analysts said the chances of a successful no-confidence vote were slim as so far only the Christian Democrats have said they would support Social Democrats.
The two parties together hold 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats. A majority of 46 votes would be needed to achieve a change of government.
The current government, a coalition of the centre-left Liberal Democrats, the conservative People's Party and the pensioners' party Desus, was elected in February and holds 49 seats.

The last time parliament passed a no-confidence vote against the government was in April 1993, when Liberal Democrat Janez Drnovsek was elected prime minister to replace Christian Democrat Lojze Peterle.
The government is expected to debate the 1997 budget proposal on Thursday but has not yet said when it plans to present it to parliament.
